facts.raw_span: A 51-year-old woman
hypothyroidism
a history of treated pulmonary tuberculosis
intermittent upper abdominal pain
dark, tarry stools
anemia (hemoglobin 11.0 g/dL)
a positive fecal occult blood test
a 103 × 46.6 mm submucosal mass on the lesser curvature of the stomach
normal overlying mucosa
a low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins confined to the submucosal layer
a vascular signal extending from the periphery into the center of the lesion
a 102 × 56.3 × 46.6 mm gastric mass without evidence of additional masses or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: The presence of a submucosal mass with a low-echo lesion and a vascular signal is unusual and points towards a GIST.

concepts.why: The presence of a submucosal mass with normal overlying mucosa is unusual and points towards a gastric leiomyoma.

a positive fecal occult blood test
contradict_spans: a low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins confined to the submucosal layer
concepts.why: The presence of dark, tarry stools and a positive fecal occult blood test is unusual and could point towards a gastric carcinoid tumor.

support_spans: intermittent upper abdominal pain
a positive fecal occult blood test
contradict_spans: a 102 × 56.3 × 46.6 mm gastric mass without evidence of additional masses or lymphadenopathy
concepts.why: The presence of intermittent upper abdominal pain and a positive fecal occult blood test is unusual and could point towards a gastric adenocarcinoma.
The gastric mass without evidence of additional masses or lymphadenopathy is consistent with a gastric schwannoma, a rare benign tumor.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a submucosal mass with a vascular signal and a low-echo lesion with regular, clear margins confined to the submucosal layer, as seen in the endoscopic ultrasound, specifically supports the diagnosis of Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST).
